errors.why: ཡན་ལག here is the member (avayava) of the proof statement: the point is that 'oneself/intended' in the definition serves to exclude, not to be part of the thesis-member; 'supplementary parts' obscures the logical term.

note: A dense Pramāṇa subcommentary rendered broadly in sequence but often loosely; the argument can be followed only with the Tibetan at hand.

errors.why: This is a quoted root-verse line ('therefore cognition has two forms'), not a section heading; turning it into a heading detaches it from the commentary that glosses it.

errors.english: because others are deluded, the world is deceived
errors.why: The Tibetan says the deluded (those confused about the beyond/other) deceive the world, i.e. they are the agents of deception, not that the world is deceived because others are deluded.

note: Sound on the self-awareness and two-aspect argument overall, but the verse/commentary boundary is blurred and a few clauses are loosely construed.
A faithful and well-annotated rendering of Karṇakagomin's argument against the universal as an unnecessary intermediary.

errors.english: because that external entity has already been clarified
errors.why: In context (cf. བཀག་ཏུ་ཟིན་ཀྱང་ just after, and the edition note) the reading is བསལ་ཟིན་ 'has already been refuted/eliminated', not 'clarified'.

note: Accurate rendering of the rebirth argument from homogeneous seeds and its formal syllogism, with one likely misreading.

errors.english: The directions are thoroughly permeated from above.
errors.why: Completing the earthquake description from the previous side, the Tibetan says the (outer) directions rise upward, not that they are permeated from above.

errors.english: Come, O Sheep-Lord, look upon the bulls!
errors.why: The formula is the Vedic invocation naming Medhātithi (medhātither meṣa, 'ram of Medhātithi'); the English invents a gloss that treats a proper name as a description.

note: A lively and largely accurate rendering of the drama scene with the rākṣasa's entrance; speakers and stage directions are correctly assigned.

errors.english: she feigned sleep [note: original: (gnyid brdzun)], and I was occupied with gazing at her face
errors.why: The roles are likely reversed: the prince feigned sleep and she was absorbed in gazing at his face, which is why she then shows embarrassment (ངོ་ཚས) when he suddenly opens his eyes and laughs.

errors.english: feeling insulted because of the king's favor toward Norzang
errors.why: The Tibetan speaks of contempt for (Suvrata's) attendance on Norzang, not of the king's favor toward Norzang; the king is not mentioned.

note: The courtly verse and narrative are readable, but who does what in the love scene and in the Brahmins' rivalry is partly misassigned.

errors.english: This should certainly be my wife.
errors.why: The king concludes that she is surely the ascetic's wife (as the next side's question confirms), not that she should become his own wife.

note: A fluent and largely faithful jātaka rendering; one misread thought of the king.

errors.english: Therefore, his wisdom should be analyzed and realized through dedicated effort.
errors.why: The root verse (PV II) says his knowledge regarding what is to be practised (anuṣṭheya) is what must be examined; 'dedicated effort' is the object of the knowledge, not the manner of analysis.

fix.find: Therefore, his wisdom should be analyzed and realized through dedicated effort.
fix.replace: Therefore, his knowledge of what is to be practised should be examined.

errors.english: The teaching that satisfies the ignorant by distinguishing agents and other factors
errors.why: The Tibetan shows that we are content with not knowing (his knowledge) through its particular distinctions, not that a teaching satisfies ignorant people.

errors.english: it is possible to know other objects; there is no difference in the non-deceptive nature regarding the essential point
errors.why: This clause gives the reason why knowing other objects cannot be established (unlike knowledge of karma and result, it is not marked by non-deception on the principal aim); the English presents it as an assertion that such knowledge is possible.

errors.english: To show how the omniscience that makes non-deceptive the essential point of the knowledge to be pursued is identified
errors.why: The Tibetan says that omniscience is NOT the criterion (only non-deception on the principal aim is); the negation is lost.

note: The PV II argument about which knowledge of the Teacher matters is repeatedly misconstrued; the verses are recognizable but the commentary's logic is not reliable.
A clear and faithful rendering of the argument against the body as the cause of mind, with verses and commentary correctly separated.

errors.english: if one keeps it after the time for wearing such robes has passed
errors.why: In this Vinaya context བགོ་བ is the distribution of robes (cīvara-bhājana); the rule concerns keeping rains-acquisitions past the robe-distribution time, not the 'time for wearing'.

note: A competent rendering of the ātyayika-robe and forest-dweller rules; the only slip is reading 'distribute' as 'wear'.
